exercise.name: Bent Knee Back to Side Kick

reference.title: Bent Knee Back to Side Kick
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; page could not be read at authoring time, movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (bent-knee hip extension, then hip abduction)

breathing.pattern: Exhale on each kick, inhale as the knee comes back under the hip.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s back, 0.8 s return, 1.2 s side, 1.2 s down

prescription.tempo: Controlled, short pause at each end
prescription.progression: Pauses at each end, then an ankle weight, then a mini band above the knees once that gear is available

cues.text: On all fours: hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat.
Knee bent 90 degrees, press the right sole up toward the ceiling until the thigh is level.
Squeeze the glute; hips stay square, no low back arch.
Bring the knee back under the hip without touching down.
Lift the bent leg out to the side, knee and foot at about the same height.
Lower the knee to just touch the mat; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back on the back kick
mistakes.fix: Stop when the thigh is level; brace the abdomen.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning the trunk away on the side lift
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders and hips square; lift only as high as you can without leaning.
Keep the knee at about 90 degrees throughout.
Pause at each end and move under control.

kinematics.norm: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips (clinical opinion)
Thigh level with the trunk at the back kick (clinical opinion; Selkowitz 2013)
Thigh out toward level with the floor at the side kick (clinical opinion; Macadam 2015)
About 1.2 s each way with short pauses (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #10856, Bent Knee Back to Side Kick, video (movement reference)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)
Macadam, Cronin & Contreras 2015, gluteal muscle activity in dynamic hip abduction and hip external rotation exercise: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 10(5):573-591; PMC4595911)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Wrist pain on all fours: use fists or forearms on a bench or box.
Knee pain kneeling: pad the knees with a folded mat.
modify: Smaller range on the side lift.
Pause on the mat between the two kicks.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives the back kick (bent-knee hip extension); quadruped hip extension ranks among the better bodyweight gluteus maximus exercises (Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Lifts the thigh out to the side (abduction with the hip flexed); the fire hydrant pattern loads the gluteus medius and upper gluteus maximus (Macadam 2015).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; the bent knee keeps them short so the glute does most of the work (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the pelvis level over the supporting knee (Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk flat and the pelvis from rotating.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keep the shoulder blades flat on the ribs.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keep the shoulder blades flat on the ribs.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keep the elbows soft and locked out under load.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keep the elbows soft and locked out under load.

guides.label: Knee path: back, then out to the side
